Livers ''' (born July 28, 1998) is an American [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Michigan Wolverines men's basketball|Michigan Wolverines]]. He attended [[Kalamazoo Central High School]] where he won the [[Mr. Basketball of Michigan]]. He was part of the [[2017–18 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|2017–18 team]] that won the [[2018 Big Ten Conference Men's Basketball Tournament]] and reached the [[2018 NCAA Division I Men's Basketball Championship Game|Championship Game]] of the [[2018 NCAA Division I Men's Basketball Tournament]]. ==Early life and high school career== Livers was born on July 28, 1998 in [[Kalamazoo, Michigan]] to Angela and Morris Livers.{{cite web|url=http://mgoblue.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=15234|title=4 Isaiah Livers|website=MGoBlue.com|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|accessdate=March 13, 2018}} He started playing basketball at the age of five with his father in the driveway.{{cite web|url=http://highschoolsports.mlive.com/news/article/-185104844948235807/michigan-signee-isaiah-livers-of-kalamazoo-central-is-2017-mr-basketball/|title=Michigan signee Isaiah Livers of Kalamazoo Central is 2017 Mr. Basketball|accessdate=January 13, 2018|date=March 20, 2017|publisher=[[MLive.com]]|author=Purcell, Jared}} Michigan began recruiting Livers in May 2016 and he made his official visit on July 28, earning an offer.{{cite web|url=http://www.mlive.com/wolverines/index.ssf/2016/08/4-star_kalamazoo_central_forwa.html|title=Isaiah Livers, a 4-star 2017 forward from Kalamazoo Central, commits to Michigan|accessdate=January 13, 2018|date=August 7, 2016|publisher=[[MLive.com]]|author=Quinn, Brendan F.}} At the end of his recruitment, he was considering visiting [[California Golden Bears men's basketball|Cal]], but decided to cancel the visit and commit to Michigan.{{cite web|url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/college/university-michigan/wolverines/2016/08/09/michigan-basketball-isaiah-livers/88448218/|title=New Michigan basketball commit Isaiah Livers says he's perfect fit|accessdate=January 13, 2018|date=August 9, 2016|work=[[Detroit Free Press]]|author=Snyder, Mark}} On August 7, 2016, Livers committed to Michigan over contenders Michigan State, Butler, Minnesota, California, and Boston College.{{cite web|url=http://www.mlive.com/wolverines/index.ssf/2016/08/4-star_kalamazoo_central_forwa.html|title=Isaiah Livers, a 4-star 2017 forward from Kalamazoo Central, commits to Michigan|accessdate=August 9, 2016|date=August 7, 2016|website=[[MLive.com]]|author=Quinn, Brendan F.}}{{cite web|url=http://insider.espn.com/blog/ncbrecruiting/on-the-trail/insider/post?id=16077|title=Scout's Take: ESPN 100 PF Isaiah Livers to Michigan|accessdate=August 9, 2016|date=August 7, 2016|publisher=[[ESPN]]|author=Rankin, Reggie}} Livers signed his [[National Letter of Intent]] to Michigan as part of a three-scholarship player incoming class with [[Jordan Poole]] and Eli Brooks.{{cite web|url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/college/university-michigan/wolverines/2016/11/11/michigan-basketball-signing/93664876/|title=Michigan basketball officially announces 2017 class|accessdate=January 13, 2018|date=November 11, 2016|work=[[Detroit Free Press]]|author=Snyder, Mark}} He was named 2017 Michigan [[Gatorade Basketball Player of the Year|Gatorade Player of the Year]] and [[Mr. Basketball of Michigan]].{{cite web|url=http://highschoolsports.mlive.com/news/article/8321932720220346426/kalamazoo-centrals-isaiah-livers-wins-michigan-gatorade-player-of-the-year-honors/|title=Kalamazoo Central's Isaiah Livers wins Michigan Gatorade Player of the Year honors|accessdate=March 22, 2017|date=March 20, 2017|work=[[MLive.com]]|author=Nothaft, Patrick}} Livers edged out second-place finisher Xavier Tillman by a 2,811–2,739 vote margin, although Tillman received three more first-place ballots. It was the closest vote in Mr. Basketball of Michigan history.{{cite web|url=http://www.detroitnews.com/story/sports/high-school/2017/03/20/isaiah-livers-named-michigan-mr-basketball/99413670/|title=Isaiah Livers named Michigan Mr. Basketball|accessdate=January 13, 2018|date=March 20, 2017|work=[[Detroit News]]|author=Goricki, David}} Livers is Michigan's 11th Mr. Basketball of Michigan, but the first since [[Manny Harris]] in 2007.{{cite web|url=http://www.mgoblue.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/032117aaf.html|title=Incoming Recruit Livers Named Michigan's Mr. Basketball|accessdate=March 22, 2017|date=March 21, 2017|website=MGoBlue.com|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]}} ==College career== ===Freshman=== [[File:20180206 UM-NW Isaiah Livers 7DM26427.jpg|thumb|upright|left|Livers for the [[2017–18 Michigan web|url=http://www.detroitnews.com/story/sports/college/university-michigan/2018/01/03/ums-isaiah-livers-relishes-breakout-performance/109133658/|title=UM’s Isaiah Livers relishes breakout starting lineup for Michigan when they faced [[2017–18 Michigan State Spartans men's basketball team|Michigan State]] in their [[Michigan–Michigan State men's basketball rivalry|rivalry game]] on January 13.{{cite web|url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/college/university-michigan/wolverines/2018/01/12/michigan-wolverines-basketball-isaiah-livers-michigan-state/1030000001/|title=Michigan web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/college-basketball-rankings-ohio-state-michigan-enter-coaches-poll-top-25/|title=College basketball rankings: Ohio State, Michigan enter defeated [[2018–19 Northwestern Wildcats men's basketball team|Northwestern]] to establish a school record for best start at 17–0 and tied the school's record 17-game win streak.{{cite web|url=http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401082459|title=No. 2 Michigan now 17-0 after 80-60 win over Northwestern|accessdate=January 14, 2019|date=January 13, web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2019/1/13/mens-basketball-career-nights-from-simpson-teske-spark-u-m-to-victory-program-best-17-0-start.aspx|title=Career Nights from Simpson, Teske Spark U-M to [[2018–19 Nebraska Cornhuskers men's basketball team|Nebraska]] 82–53. Livers made his first start of the season, replacing an injured [[Charles Matthews (basketball)|Charles Matthews]], and posted 12 points and 10 assists, for his first career double-double.{{cite web|url=http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401082468|title=No. 9 Michigan beats Nebraska 82-53 in home finale|accessdate=February 28, 2019|date=February 28, web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2019/2/28/mens-basketball-michigan-dominates-from-start-to-finish-against-nebraska-on-senior-night.aspx|title=Michigan Dominates from Start to Finish Against Nebraska web|url=http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401120738|title=Livers scores 21, No. 10 Michigan pounds Minnesota 76-49|accessdate=March 16, 2019|date=March 16, Title Game|accessdate=March 16, 2019|date=March 16, 2019|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|website=MGoBlue.com|author=Wywrot, Tom}} ===Junior=== On November 12, Michigan defeated [[2019–20 Creighton Bluejays men's basketball team|Creighton]] 79–69 in the [[Gavitt Tipoff Games]] behind a then career-high 22 points from Livers.{{cite web|url=http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401166058|title=Strong second half lifts Michigan past Creighton 79-69|accessdate=November 12, 2019|date=November 12, 2019|publisher=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]}}{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2019/11/12/mens-basketball-livers-career-night-leads-michigan-past-creighton.aspx|title=Livers' Career Night Leads Michigan Past Creighton|first=Tom|last=Wywrot|accessdate=November 12, 2019|date=November 12, 2019|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|website=MGoBlue.com}} On November 22, Michigan defeated [[2019–20 Houston Baptist Huskies men's basketball team|Houston Baptist]] 111–68 behind a career-high 24 points by Livers. Michigan's 111 points were the most points scored in a game since a 112–64 victory over [[1997–98 Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball team|Indiana]] in [[1997–98 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|1998]].{{cite web|url=http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401166090|title=Livers scores 24, Michigan routs Houston Baptist, 111-68|accessdate=November 22, 2019|date=November 22, 2019|publisher=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]}}{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2019/11/22/mens-basketball-simpsons-career-night-leads-michigan-to-rout-of-houston-baptist.aspx|title=Simpson's Career Night Leads Michigan to Rout of Houston Baptist|first=Tom|last=Wywrot|accessdate=November 22, 2019|date=November 22, 2019|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|website=MGoBlue.com}} He suffered a groin injury on December 21 in a win over [[Presbyterian Blue Hose men's basketball|Presbyterian]].{{cite news |title=Michigan forward Isaiah Livers out indefinitely with groin injury |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/28379234/michigan-forward-isaiah-livers-indefinitely-groin-injury |accessdate=December 30, 2019 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=December 27, 2019}} He missed nine of the next 10 games before facing [[2019–20 Michigan State Spartans men's basketball team|Michigan State]] on February 8.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401166214|title=Livers returns, Michigan beats No. 16 Michigan State 77-68|accessdate=February 9, 2020|date=February 8, 2020|publisher=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]}} On February 16, Livers suffered an ankle injury against [[2019–20 Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball team|Indiana]] and missed the following game against [[2019–20 Rutgers Scarlet Knights men's basketball team|Rutgers]]. In his return versus [[2019–20 Purdue Boilermakers men's basketball team|Purdue]], Livers had 19 points, six rebounds, two blocks and a steal in a 71-63 victory.{{cite news |last1=Sang |first1=Orion |title=Michigan basketball crossing fingers that Isaiah Livers' injury streak is over |url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/college/university-michigan/wolverines/2020/02/24/michigan-basketball-isaiah-livers-injury/4852612002/ |accessdate=February 28, 2020 |work=[[Detroit Free Press]] |date=February 24, 2020}} On March 5, Michigan defeated [[2019–20 Nebraska Cornhuskers men's basketball team|Nebraska]] 82–58, as Livers posted 18 points and ten rebounds, for his second career double-double.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401166262|title=No. 25 Michigan beats Nebraska 82-58 with Beilein on hand|accessdate=March 5, 2020|date=March 5, 2020|publisher=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]}}{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2020/3/5/mens-basketball-wolverines-rout-nebraska-for-senior-day-win.aspx|title=Wolverines Rout Nebraska for Senior Day Win|first=Tom|last=Wywrot|accessdate=March 5, 2020|date=March 5, 2020|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|website=MGoBlue.com}} At the close of the regular season, Livers was named Honorable Mention All-Big Ten by the media.{{cite press release|url=https://bigten.org/news/2020/3/9/big-ten-unveils-mens-basketball-postseason-honors-on-btn.aspx|title=Big Ten Unveils Men’s Basketball Postseason Honors on BTN|publisher=[[Big Ten Conference]] |date=March 9, 2020 |accessdate=March 9, 2020}} Livers started 21 games and averaged 12.9 points per game while shooting 40 percent from behind the arc. He missed only two free-throws the entire season, making 44-for-46 (.957) from the line.{{Cite web|date=2020-07-17|title=Isaiah Livers announces return to Michigan basketball for 2020-21|url=https://wolverineswire.usatoday.com/2020/07/17/michigan-basketball-isaiah-livers-to-return-for-senior-season/|access-date=2020-07-17|website=WolverinesWire|language=en}} Following the season he declared for the [[2020 NBA draft]] but did not hire an agent and left the door open to return for his senior season.{{cite news |last1=Kahn |first1=Andrew |title=Michigan junior Isaiah Livers declares for NBA draft |url=https://www.mlive.com/wolverines/2020/03/michigan-junior-isaiah-livers-declares-for-nba-draft.html |accessdate=March 31, 2020 |work=MLive |date=March 30, 2020}} On July 17, 2020, Livers announced that he would return to Michigan for his senior season.{{Cite web|last=Sang|first=Orion|title=Michigan basketball gets big boost with Isaiah Livers returning for his senior year|url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/college/university-michigan/wolverines/2020/07/17/michigan-basketball-isaiah-livers-nba-draft/5459872002/|access-date=2020-07-17|website=Detroit Free Press|language=en}} ===Senior=== During his senior season, Livers posted 16 double-figure games with a team-high five 20+ point games, and averaged 13.9 points per game. Livers made a team-high 50 three-pointers, reaching 50+ in a season for the second time in his career. He averaged a career-best 6.2 rebounds and 2.0 assists, and he added a pair of double-doubles. Following the season, he was named second-team All-Big Ten by the coaches and media.{{cite web |url=https://bigten.org/news/2021/3/9/general-2020-21-big-ten-mens-basketball-postseason-honors-announced.aspx |title=2020-21 Big Ten Men’s Basketball Postseason Honors Announced |website=BigTen.org |date=March 9, 2021 |access-date=March 9, 2021}}{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2021/3/9/mens-basketball-dickinson-howard-headline-big-ten-awards-as-top-freshman-coach.aspx |title=Dickinson, Howard Headline Big Ten Awards as Top Freshman, Coach |first=Tom |last=Wywrot |accessdate=March 9, 2021 |date=March 9, 2021 |publisher=[[CBS Interactive]] |website=MGoBlue.com}} On March 13, 2021, Livers suffered a stress injury to his right foot during a quarterfinal game against [[Maryland Terrapins men's basketball|Maryland]] in the [[2021 Big Ten Men's Basketball Tournament|2021 Big Ten Tournament]] which sidelined him indefinitely.{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2021/3/13/mens-basketball-livers-out-indefinitely-with-stress-injury-to-right-foot.aspx |title=Livers Out Indefinitely with Stress Injury to Right Foot |first=Tom |last=Wywrot |accessdate=March 13, 2021 |date=March 13, 2021 |publisher=[[CBS Interactive]] |website=MGoBlue.com}} On April 2, 2021, Livers underwent successful surgery on his foot and recovery time is expected to be a minimum of six months.{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2021/4/2/mens-basketball-livers-undergoes-successful-surgery-on-right-foot.aspx |title=Livers Undergoes Successful Surgery on Right Foot |first=Tom |last=Wywrot
